_comment: When an instrument must be registered under the Registration Act, 1908, and what follows if it is not. Previously this lived as a boolean on three document types in domainRegistry.js, tested by searching the draft text for words like 'sub-registrar' -- which asked whether the document TALKS about registration, not whether registration is legally required. Reviewed and maintained by the supervising advocate.
consequence: An instrument requiring registration that is not registered cannot be received in evidence of any transaction affecting the immovable property it relates to, and confers no power to adjudge.

always_registrable.statutory_reference: Registration Act, 1908 - S.17(1)(a); Transfer of Property Act, 1882 - S.123
Registration Act, 1908 - S.17(1)(b); Transfer of Property Act, 1882 - S.59

term_triggered.statutory_reference: Registration Act, 1908 - S.17(1)(d); Transfer of Property Act, 1882 - S.107
term_triggered.at_or_above: A lease of immovable property from year to year, or for any term exceeding one year, must be registered.
term_triggered.below: A lease for a term of less than one year is not compulsorily registrable, though it may still attract stamp duty.

state_overrides.reason: In Maharashtra a leave and licence agreement must be registered regardless of its term, and the licensor bears the responsibility for effecting registration.

state_notes.Maharashtra: Registration is effected before the Sub-Registrar; leave and licence agreements are registrable under S.55 of the Maharashtra Rent Control Act, 1999 regardless of term.
